findings.checklist_item: Pin the guard PLACEMENT so the capability-absent branch runs before the _computed increment (guard at function/loop entry, short-circuiting the whole comment/link phase including the get_issue_links dedup probe), and reconcile AC1's 'before the call' wording with AC2b's 'increments neither computed nor applied'.
evidence: AC1: 'runtime-guarded with isinstance ... before the call'
AC2b: 'The capability-absent path increments NEITHER *_computed NOR *_applied'
findings.finding: AC1 specifies the isinstance guard goes 'before the call', but the live counters _comments_computed (dispatch_apply_phases.py:162) and _links_computed (dispatch_one.py:739) increment BEFORE the guarded call site; a guard placed literally 'before the call' but AFTER the counter would still increment _computed on the capability-absent path, contradicting AC2b's requirement that the absent path increment NEITHER computed NOR applied (and would then trip the silent-no-op canary AC2b says must stay silent).
scenarios: A DC transport lacking SupportsComments/SupportsLinks: guard placed at the call site (after the per-entry counter) records _computed>0, applied==0, tripping apply_handlers' silent-no-op canary that AC2b asserts must stay silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC1 to require the isinstance guard gate the entire phase before any per-entry _computed increment (and before the link dedup probe at dispatch_one.py:722), rather than merely 'before the call', so a capability-absent transport short-circuits with computed==0/applied==0 as AC2b demands.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the lifecycle of the new capability-absent alert kinds in bridge_alerts: whether they are deduped/upserted per (kind,site) or accumulate per pass, and their retirement/cleanup path, given a non-capable backend triggers them on every reconcile pass.
evidence: 'the sub-op still counted as computed ... and a durable record on the EXISTING bridge_alerts channel (pass_io._load_alert_store()) ... under a distinct kind: outbound-comment-capability-absent / outbound-link-capability-absent'

'It matters now because the capability Protocols exist precisely so a SECOND backend (DC) may not implement them.' — a DC backend lacking the capability is a permanent condition, so the durable record fires every pass, not once.
ABSENCE: no RETIRE/dedupe/idempotency lifecycle stated for the new kinds; existing divergence/reporter alerts may be event-driven rather than per-pass-recurring.
findings.finding: The plan writes a durable capability-absent record to the shared `bridge_alerts` store on a condition (a backend that does not implement the capability, e.g. DC) that is DESIGNED and PERMANENT — it recurs on every reconcile pass — yet the plan does not specify whether these new-kind records are deduped, bounded, or retired, risking unbounded accumulation in that store.
findings.location: OPERATOR DECISION → 'Capability absent → ... a durable record on the EXISTING bridge_alerts channel'
findings.suggested_fix: State that capability-absent records are keyed by (kind, site) and upserted (or emitted at most once per pass/run), mirroring how record_parent_divergence handles recurrence, and note the store's existing retention/retirement behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the `_call_with_retry` consumer inventory with find_referencing_symbols AND a string grep, then extend AC9 to include the LSP-invisible patch.object sites (test_applier_clean_label.py:63 -> apply_inbound._call_with_retry; test_apply_outbound_create_rollback.py:78 -> apply_outbound._call_with_retry) and name apply_inbound/apply_inbound_records as affected re-export nodes.
evidence: Plan: "dispatch_one re-exports the name, so dispatch_one._call_with_retry (...) and batch_dispatch._call_with_retry (test_error_taxonomy.py:68) keep resolving, as do applier/apply_outbound's imports."
AC9 names only: test_retry_httperror.py, test_error_taxonomy.py, test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py, test_timeout_s_forwarding_heldout_7504.py
findings.finding: The `_call_with_retry` relocation inventory omits string-based `patch.object` consumers and one re-export hop. The plan lists dispatch_one/batch_dispatch/applier/apply_outbound as the consumers that must keep resolving and names four regression tests in AC9, but a string grep for `_call_with_retry` surfaces two dynamic patch sites the symbol graph will not: `patch.object(apply_inbound, "_call_with_retry", ...)` (test_applier_clean_label.py:63) and `patch.object(apply_outbound, "_call_with_retry", ...)` (test_apply_outbound_create_rollback.py:78). `apply_inbound` (and apply_inbound_records) bind the name via `from batch_dispatch import _call_with_retry`, a re-export hop the plan does not list as affected; the relocation lengthens that chain (dispatch_apply_phases -> dispatch_one re-export -> batch_dispatch re-export -> apply_inbound).
findings.location: Module-size constraint (drives one relocation) paragraph; AC9
scenarios: test_applier_clean_label.py patches apply_inbound._call_with_retry by string; if the re-export chain through batch_dispatch->dispatch_one is not preserved for the relocated symbol, patch.object raises AttributeError and the test breaks — and it is not in AC9's regression list, so the breakage is unguarded.
test_apply_outbound_create_rollback.py patches apply_outbound._call_with_retry by string; same LSP-invisible failure mode, also absent from AC9.
apply_inbound_records.py also imports _call_with_retry from batch_dispatch; it is an affected re-export consumer the inventory does not enumerate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add test_applier_clean_label.py and test_apply_outbound_create_rollback.py to AC9's unmodified-pass list, and state that the dispatch_one re-export must remain so batch_dispatch's re-export (consumed by apply_inbound, apply_inbound_records, apply_outbound) keeps `_call_with_retry` bound for the string-based patch.object sites.
